cases.narrative: A 2015 Tesla Model S struck a parked Snohomish County sheriff's patrol vehicle in Arlington, Washington, while a deputy was attending an earlier collision with his emergency lights on. Washington State Patrol said the driver told troopers the car was in Autopilot mode and that he assumed it would slow and move over. No one was injured; the sheriff's department reported significant damage to the patrol car.

cases.narrative: On April 25, 2019, a 2019 Tesla Model S with Autopilot engaged ran a stop sign at about 62 mph at a T-intersection on Card Sound Road near Key Largo, Florida, and struck a parked SUV, which hit two people standing nearby; one was killed and one seriously injured. The driver, who had looked down to retrieve a dropped phone, was cited for careless driving and pleaded no contest, with adjudication withheld. In August 2025 a federal jury found Tesla 33% responsible; Tesla's share of the judgment is about $243 million. Tesla filed an appeal brief on November 6, 2026, arguing the distracted driver caused the crash; the appeals court has not ruled.
